historical_context: M13/40 was Italy's primary medium tank in North Africa. Equipped Ariete Division's tank battalions. Adequate against lighter British tanks but outclassed by Matilda II. Sand filter problems plagued early operations.

M13/40.notes: Vulnerable to British tanks. Sand filter problems caused mechanical failures in April 1941.

strengths: Adequate against British cruiser tanks at range
Supported by Italian artillery and infantry
Improved reliability after sand filter fixes (May 1941+)
weaknesses: Outclassed by British Matilda II (47mm cannot penetrate)
Sand filter problems in April 1941 (only 7 reached Tobruk on 11 April)
Italian crew training inferior to British/German
tactical_notes.typical_deployment: Support Italian infantry divisions. Best used in defensive positions or against lighter British tanks. Avoid engagements with Matilda II. Coordinate with German armor when possible. Improved performance after May 1941 when sand filter issues resolved.

phase_6_data_source.battalions: III, V, VII, VIII Battaglione Carri M
phase_6_data_source.operational_notes: Strength increased from 75-85 in April to 99+ by June. Sand filters caused only 7 tanks operational for 11 April Tobruk assault.
phase_6_data_source.historical_success: Successfully penetrated Tobruk perimeter on 1 May 1941, capturing strongpoints R3-R7
